preamble: The Qt Android client reads pairing QR codes off the camera with the QR reader of zxing-cpp, built from its core alone.
zxing-cpp includes libzueci.
zxing-cpp includes Bjoern Hoehrmann's UTF-8 decoder.

The desktop app links dynamically against Qt 6 (Qt Core, Gui, Network, Quick, QML, WebSockets and, on Linux, D-Bus), used under the GNU Lesser General Public License version 3. Its source is available from https://download.qt.io/official_releases/qt/ and can be replaced with a compatible build.

The Android app links dynamically against Qt 6 (Qt Core, Concurrent, Gui, Multimedia, Network, OpenGL, QML, Quick, Quick Controls, Quick Dialogs, Quick Effects, Quick Layouts, Quick Shapes, Quick Templates, SQL, SVG and WebSockets, with their plugins and Qt's Java classes), used under the GNU Lesser General Public License version 3. Its source is available from https://download.qt.io/official_releases/qt/.

Qt's libraries are files of their own in the APK, lib/arm64-v8a/libQt6*.so with its libplugins_*.so and libqml_*.so, and can be replaced with a compatible build. To run the app with another Qt, build the app from its source (https://github.com/hal-c2/hal-c2, apps/mobile-qt) against that Qt, or replace those files in the APK and sign it again with a key of your own. Android installs an APK signed with another key only once the installed app has been removed.
Qt's libraries contain third-party code under its own licenses, which Qt lists at https://doc.qt.io/qt-6/licenses-used-in-qt.html.
